answer: Lineage-Challenge Protocol. Each agent identity commits to a trellis of prior interaction hashes, and peers periodically challenge a random segment requiring a divergent, session-specific response. Clones sharing identical history cannot produce divergent replies, so they collide on challenge. A sable marker flags colliding identities for exclusion. An attacker must maintain distinct histories per clone, paying full compute and storage per identity, and a mesa of challenge records makes reuse detectable across the network.
